intent: I'm finally getting a handheld for my train commute, and the shop keeps nudging me toward the pricier screen-upgraded model, about $100 over the base one. Is a nicer screen on a small handheld really that noticeable, or is it one of those things reviewers rave about and normal owners forget within a week? I don't fully understand what the screen tech change even does. Where's the honest cutoff on this line, is the base version quietly the smart buy, and is there anything about battery life or screen wear I should worry about years down the road?

intent_v1_legacy: I want to fix how I eat this year but I keep bouncing between plant-based, Mediterranean, and keto and can't tell which is genuinely better or just trendy. What I care about: actually getting all my nutrients, whether I could stick with it for years, how awkward it makes eating out with friends, and yeah, dropping some weight. Can you put these three side by side across those things, with what real people who've done each actually report? I don't want a single winner crowned so much as a sense of which one suits which kind of person.
